title: A Pending Property Title Dispute Cannot Be Used to Deny an Electricity Connection: Allahabad High Court
case_name: Rakesh Kumar Mishra v. State of U.P. through Principal Secretary, Energy Deptt., Lko. & 4 Others
card_summary: Justices Alok Mathur and Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary allowed a writ petition by Rakesh Kumar Mishra, whose power connection application for a Raebareli property was rejected for want of a sale deed, succession certificate or NOC, while a title dispute over the property was pending in civil court. The court held electricity access is protected under Article 21 and cannot be denied solely for a pending ownership dispute.
card_tip: An electricity connection can be secured on proof of occupancy alone, such as an indemnity form, lease deed or rent receipt, even while a title dispute is pending; a civil title dispute is not a bar.
verification_notes: LiveLaw, The Print and Free Press Journal agree on the bench, the Raebareli facts, the Article 21 holding, the Electricity Supply Code occupancy-proof route, and the ten-day direction for fresh consideration. LawChakra and The Law Communicants corroborate the same holding. The exact pronouncement date was not stated in the reports seen; 21 October 2026 is taken from the citation's upload date (2026 LiveLaw (AB) 866) and sits within the reported publication window of 21-22 October 2026.
